docs.title: Home
docs.text:
Scarlet Composer Studio

Distributed shared memory and communication primitives for decentralized Agentic-AI — Redis backend, Apache 2.0, built for the edge.

Component What it does Mapper Distributed key-value store. Workers write independently; any node reads all values with AllGather or folds them with Reduce. Federator One-line federated aggregation. Workers post local models; the head calls Aggregate to sum, multiply, or max across all contributions. Messenger Reliable per-agent inboxes with sequence-numbered delivery, a liveness registry, and heartbeat threads — all over raw Redis. Harness A decentralized Skill runtime built on the primitives above: a head dispatches work, workers coordinate, and agents find each other's data by feature, not by connection string. Composer UI Operator dashboard to deploy scarlets, browse the agent registry, manage data sources, and stream logs — from a browser. LLM / MCP ready Messenger.AsTools() exports MCP-compatible tool definitions. Drop into any agent framework: LangChain, LlamaIndex, Open WebUI.

Designed for physically distributed, edge-first deployments — industrial and IoT sites with no cloud dependency, just Redis on your own network.

docs.title: Architecture at a Glance
docs.text:
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  scarlet-composer  (operator UI)                              │
│  composer-ui (Next.js, :3000)  ⇄  composer-api (FastAPI)       │
│  background-server — node identity resolution                 │
└───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                                │
┌───────────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
│                             Redis                              │
│      Mapper data     Messenger queues     Scarlet definitions   │
└───────────────────────────────▲────────────────────────────────┘
                                │
┌───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┐
│  scarlet-agents  (harness)              scarlets  (library)     │
│  Skill dispatch, AgentDialogue,         Mapper / Federator /    │
│  local-first data access                Messenger — imported    │
│                                          directly, no broker     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Four packages ship from this repository:

Package What it contains scarlets Mapper, Federator, Messenger, RedisScarlet, ScarletBase, RedisContract, ScarletUtils, RedisLogger scarletcomposer composer-api (FastAPI) + composer-ui (Next.js) operator dashboard, ScarletInterpreter, scarlet-composer CLI data-connectors Pluggable data-source connectors (MSSQL, Postgres, MySQL, PI, InfluxDB, Redis, CSV, Excel) harness/ The agentic Skill runtime — see Harness

Agent containers only need scarlets. The operator dashboard needs scarletcomposer. Agents built with the harness also need data-connectors for local-mode data sources.

docs.title: vs. A2A and ACP
docs.text:
A2A and ACP answer: how does one agent call another?

Scarlet Composer answers: how do many agents share state and coordinate across machines they physically own?

A2A / ACP Scarlet Composer Model Request-response (HTTP) Shared memory + messaging Topology Point-to-point Many-to-many via shared primitives State Stateless Persistent in Redis Aggregation Manual (N HTTP round trips) AllGather / Reduce built in Data sovereignty Cloud-mediated Operator-controlled LLM integration Yes Yes — AsTools() / MCP

They are complementary.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome — bug reports, documentation improvements, new examples, and feature additions.

docs.title: Development Setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/disys-lab/scarlet-composer-studio
cd scarlet-composer-studio

# Install both packages in editable mode
pip install -e .

# Install test dependencies
pip install pytest requests

Set environment variables for your development Redis:

export REDIS_HOST=localhost
export REDIS_PORT=6379
export REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN=your-dev-password

docs.title: Running Tests
docs.text:
The test suite requires a running Redis instance and the mock Nebula manager. Start both with Docker Compose:

docker compose -f tests/docker-compose.yml up -d
./run_tests.sh

Or run specific tests:

pytest tests/test_e2e.py -v
pytest tests/test_scarlets.py -v
pytest tests/test_background_server.py -v

All 20+ e2e tests must pass before opening a pull request.

docs.title: Test structure
docs.text: File What it tests tests/test_e2e.py Full agent lifecycle — registration, task dispatch, ordered delivery, broadcast, GatherStatus, clearAll tests/test_scarlets.py Mapper and Federator primitives tests/test_background_server.py Tornado /api/v2/getNodeInfo resolution tests/test_data_sources.py Data source UI logic

docs.title: Pull Request Guidelines
docs.text:
• Open an issue first for significant feature additions or breaking changes.
  • Match the coding style of the file you are modifying.
  • Add or update tests for any changed behaviour. All existing tests must continue to pass.
  • Keep commits focused. One logical change per commit.
  • Do not modify docs/DESIGN_v*.md files — these are internal working documents. User-facing documentation lives in docs/architecture.md, docs/api.md, and docs/deployment.md.

docs.title: Reporting Bugs
docs.text: Open a GitHub issue with: - Python version and OS - Scarlet package version (pip show scarlets) - Minimal reproduction script - Full traceback

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.9+
  • Redis 6+ with AUTH enabled
  • Docker Engine 24+ (for containerised deployments)

docs.title: Option A — pip (agents only)
docs.text:
For worker and head agent code — everything needed to use Mapper, Federator, and Messenger:

pip install scarlets

docs.title: Option B — pip (full stack)
docs.text:
For the operator dashboard and CLI as well:

pip install scarlets scarletcomposer

docs.title: Option C — from source (development)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/disys-lab/scarlet-composer-studio
cd scarlet-composer-studio

# Install both packages in editable mode
pip install -e .

# Verify
scarlet-composer --version

docs.title: Option D — Docker images
docs.text:
Pre-built images are published to ghcr.io/disys-lab/:

Image Contents ghcr.io/disys-lab/scarlet-agent-base scarlets + supervisor — the base every agent container extends ghcr.io/disys-lab/scarlet-composer composer-api (FastAPI) + composer-ui (Next.js) operator dashboard ghcr.io/disys-lab/scarlet-agents The harness — decentralized agentic Skill runtime 
# Run the Composer UI
docker run -d \
  -p 8501:3000 \
  -e REDIS_HOST=your-redis-host \
  -e REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN=your-redis-password \
  ghcr.io/disys-lab/scarlet-composer:latest

See Docker Images for build instructions and how to extend the agent base.

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text:
Set the minimum required environment variables and run a quick smoke test:

export REDIS_HOST=localhost
export REDIS_PORT=6379
export REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN=your-password
export APP_ID=test
export NODE_ADDRESS=local

from scarlets.core.Mapper import Mapper
import numpy as np

m = Mapper("smoke_test")
m.Map(np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]), key="local")
values, ok, _ = m.AllGather()
print(ok, values)   # True  {"local": array([1., 2., 3.])}
m.clearAll()

If you see True and the array, everything is wired up correctly.

docs.title: Launch the Composer UI
docs.text: The operator dashboard (composer-api + composer-ui) is a Docker image, not a pip-installed CLI command — see Option D above, or Docker Images for building it locally. The scarlet-composer CLI installed by pip install scarletcomposer covers a different job: parsing #scarlet declarations from source files (scarlet-composer composer compose <dir>) — see CLI Reference.

docs.title: Quickstart — Docker Compose
docs.text:
Stand up a complete Scarlet deployment on a single machine in under 5 minutes.

What you'll get

A Scarlet Composer UI and a live hello-agent that listens on two Messenger buses and echoes messages back. All wired together with docker compose up against an external Redis instance.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Docker Engine 24+ and Docker Compose v2
  • A Redis 6+ instance with AUTH enabled
  • Pull access to ghcr.io/disys-lab/

docs.title: Step 1 — Clone and configure
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/disys-lab/scarlet-composer-studio
cd scarlet-composer-studio/examples/quickstart
cp .env.example .env

Edit .env — the only required changes:

.env (minimum)
REDIS_HOST=your-redis-host        # or host.docker.internal for local Redis
REDIS_AUTH_TOKEN=your-redis-password

No Redis? Start one locally

docker run -d -p 6379:6379 \
  redis/redis-stack:7.4.0-v1 \
  redis-server --requirepass mypassword
Then set REDIS_HOST=host.docker.internal in .env.

docs.title: Step 2 — Start the stack
docs.text:
docker compose up --build -d
Container Role scarlet-composer Operator UI — Next.js on 8501, FastAPI bound internally hello-agent Sample agent — listens on two Messenger buses, echoes messages, heartbeats every 60 s

Watch progress: 

docker compose logs -f hello-agent

docs.title: Step 3 — Open the Composer UI
docs.text:
Visit http://localhost:8501

Redis connection details come from .env at container start — nothing to configure in the browser. With AUTH_ENABLED=false (the default here) you land straight on the dashboard.

Click Agents in the sidebar — you should see hello-agent_local with a green status indicator.

docs.title: Step 4 — Send your first message
docs.text:
From a Python REPL on any machine that can reach your Redis:

from scarlets.messaging import Messenger

sender = Messenger("quickstart_headagent", agentId="my-repl")

# hello-agent's agentId is "hello-agent_local"
sender.Send("hello-agent_local", {"task": "ping", "data": "hello world"})

reply = sender.Receive(timeout=5)
print(reply["body"])
# → {"echo": {"task": "ping", "data": "hello world"}, "from": "hello-agent_local", ...}

docs.title: Check who is online
docs.text:
print(sender.GatherStatus())
# {
#   "hello-agent_local": {
#     "status": "online",
#     "capabilities": ["echo", "heartbeat"],
#     "device_group": "quickstart_subagent",
#     "head_bus": "quickstart_headagent",
#   }
# }

docs.title: Broadcast to all agents
docs.text: sender.Broadcast({"directive": "update_config", "version": 2})

docs.title: Run the smoke test
docs.text: python3 smoke_test.py --env .env

docs.title: Step 5 — Explore the local bus
docs.text:
hello-agent also listens on quickstart_subagent for intra-group communication:

local = Messenger("quickstart_subagent", agentId="peer")
local.Send("hello-agent_local", {"task": "local-ping"})
reply = local.Receive(timeout=5)
print(reply["body"]["channel"])  # "quickstart_subagent"

docs.title: Step 6 — Tear down
docs.text: docker compose down
